gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Arctis Nova 5X's headline 60-hour battery is its Bluetooth figure: on an Xbox it has to run through its 2.4 GHz dongle, which SoundGuys reports SteelSeries rates at 50 hours and which lasted 42 h 10 min in SoundGuys' test.
standout_why: I could not read the rankings or battery numbers on the two cited rivals. RTINGS 'The 6 Best Headsets For Xbox Series X/S' (3,517 characters of text, all navigation) and Tom's Guide 'Best gaming headsets in 2026' (navigation and membership prompts, cut off) both came back without their article text. So I can't rule out that they split the Nova 5X battery claim by connection type. What ChatGPT's own answer showed, built from those pages, is the uncorrected 'up to 60-hour battery' for the Nova 5X with no mode attached. SteelSeries' own Nova 5X page also states '60-Hour Battery Life' with no condition. I did not open the uncited results, ranks 3 to 13.
decides: This doesn't change the pick, but it fixes how the Nova 5X is described. On Xbox it gets the 2.4 GHz figure: rated 50 h and measured at 42 h 10 min, which is 70% of the 60 h headline. That is still about twice the Xbox Wireless Headset's 20 h rating. It also strengthens the Turtle Beach Stealth 600 Gen 3 (Xbox) as the long-battery pick, since its 80 h claim has no Bluetooth-only qualifier on its page. Our page's 'Battery (claimed / tested)' column should show the Nova 5X as '50 h on 2.4 GHz (60 h Bluetooth) / 42 h 10 min (SoundGuys)'. The column should also note that each maker words its battery claim differently: Microsoft says its figure came from pre-production units, SteelSeries gives no mode, and Turtle Beach gives no test conditions.

findings.label: Maker's battery claim as printed
findings.value: 60 h ('60-Hour Battery Life'), no connection mode or test conditions given
findings.note: The page says a charge lasts '8 hours a day for a full week'. The SteelSeries launch blog (steelseries.com/blog/introducing-arctis-nova-5-wireless-gaming-headset-1104, 04.25.2024) also gives 60 h with no mode.

findings.label: Battery rating by connection type, as reported by SoundGuys
findings.value: 50 h on the 2.4 GHz dongle; 60 h on Bluetooth
findings.source_title: SteelSeries Arctis Nova 5X review (SoundGuys, Adam Birney, updated Mar 28, 2025)
findings.note: SoundGuys: the test result is 'less than SteelSeries' advertised 50 hours of playtime' and 'SteelSeries advertises 60 hours of playback via Bluetooth.' I could not find the 50/60 split on a SteelSeries page.

findings.label: Measured battery on the 2.4 GHz dongle (the connection used on Xbox)
findings.source_title: SteelSeries Arctis Nova 5X review (SoundGuys, Adam Birney, updated Mar 28, 2025)
findings.note: Played on a PC through the USB-C dongle at about 50% volume. 42.17 h is 70% of the 60 h headline and 84% of the 50 h 2.4 GHz rating. SoundGuys says the dongle has a switch to 'toggle between Xbox compatibility and, well, everything else', so on Xbox the headset runs on the dongle.

findings.label: 2.4 GHz and Bluetooth at the same time
findings.value: Not supported: one connection at a time, switched with a button
findings.source_title: SteelSeries Arctis Nova 5X review (SoundGuys, Adam Birney, updated Mar 28, 2025)
findings.note: SoundGuys: 'you cannot connect to both at the same time.' The SteelSeries blog describes it as 'Switch between those two connections with a tap of a button.'

findings.label: Weight (maker)
findings.note: Given in the retractable-mic section. SoundGuys' spec table says 703 g, which looks like a boxed weight, so I used the maker's figure.

findings.label: Maker's battery claim and its footnote
findings.value: Up to 20 h; footnote: 'Testing conducted by Microsoft using pre-production units' and 'Battery life varies significantly with distance from console, additional accessories, usage and other factors'
findings.note: This is the only one of the three wireless makers whose page says how the battery claim was produced. No volume level is given.

findings.label: Charge time
findings.value: 30 min of charging gives about 4 h; full charge in about 3 h
findings.note: The page adds 'when headset is not in use'.

findings.label: Maker's battery claim as printed
findings.value: 80 h ('Best-in-Class 80-Hour Battery Life with Quick Charge'), no connection mode, volume or lighting condition given
findings.source_title: Stealth 600 Wireless Gaming Headset | Turtle Beach
findings.note: The only related footnote is '*Select advanced audio features available in 2.4GHz wireless mode may not be supported in Bluetooth® mode.' No quick-charge time is given.

findings.label: Price (maker's US store)
findings.source_title: Stealth 600 Wireless Gaming Headset | Turtle Beach
findings.note: Full list price with free shipping. The page lists both Xbox Series X|S/One and PS5/PS4 compatibility; the FAQ mentions a USB-A transmitter for Xbox.
